description.narrative: Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.

Sustainable production in the Brazilian Amazon offers significant socio-economic benefits for local communities, fostering both environmental conservation and improved livelihoods. By promoting non-timber forest product harvesting practices, communities can generate diversified income streams while preserving the region's rich biodiversity. These activities reduce dependence on environmentally destructive practices like illegal logging and slash-and-burn agriculture, contributing to long-term ecological stability. Economically, sustainable production enhances food security and creates jobs. This, in turn, empowers local producers, strengthens value chains, and encourages entrepreneurship. Ultimately, sustainable production fosters resilient communities capable of thriving economically while safeguarding the Amazon's vital ecosystems. The project will increase the livelihoods of 20,000 people (number of family members of the direct beneficiaries). Economic Benefits Increased Income and Financial Inclusion: the project provide the necessary capital for cooperatives to invest in equipment, improve processing, or expand their operations. This directly leads to higher productivity and better quality products, which in turn results in higher sales and increased income for community members. Financial inclusion will be significantly enhanced, which is often a challenge in remote areas. Strengthened Value Chains: Technical assistance helps cooperatives professionalize their management, improve product quality, and meet market standards. This allows them to move beyond subsistence practices and reach new buyers/markets, reducing their dependence on intermediaries who often capture most of the profit. Job Creation and Local Economic Growth: As cooperatives grow and become more profitable, they create more jobs for community members, including women and youth, fostering a stronger local economy. This stimulates local commerce and reduces the pressure for residents to seek income in unsustainable industries like illegal logging or mining. Social and Governance Benefits Community Empowerment and Leadership: The technical assistance component focuses on building skills in business management, women and youth inclusion, governance, and financial literacy. This empowers community members—particularly women and young people—to take on leadership roles within the cooperative, strengthening local decision-making processes and organizational resilience. Preservation of Culture and Land: By providing a viable economic alternative, the project incentivizes communities to protect the standing forest and their traditional territories. This validates and strengthens traditional knowledge of natural resource management, connecting economic success to cultural and environmental preservation. Improved Quality of Life: Increased and stable income allows communities to invest in better education, health, and infrastructure, leading to a direct improvement in their overall quality of life. The success of the cooperatives also builds community cohesion and a shared sense of purpose. In essence, the Amazonia Viva project provides the tools for communities to be the primary beneficiaries of their own natural resources. It creates a self-reinforcing cycle where economic growth is directly linked to social development and environmental conservation. During project implementation the numbers of loans, value, number of families will be monitored.

The overarching goal of the project is to protect the Amazon rainforest by strengthening Amazon socio-biodiversity organizations, businesses, and supply chains, promoting a development model in the Brazilian Protected Areas System in the Amazon that empowers conservation stewards (ILPCs) by combining conservation with income generation. The estimated improvement of the effectiveness of protected areas (Resex, RDS, Flotas and APAs â€“ IUCN categories IV and VI) reaches 11.9M hectares and provides global environmental benefits. The project strategy to achieve this goal is to use a non-grant instrument to support a common financial instrument in Brazil (CRA - agribusiness receivables certificate) innovatively, for the first time for sustainable production in the Amazon and leveraging Natura (Brazilian major cosmetic industry) strong and trusting relationship of 20 years built with local cooperatives.
